V2_E4.note: reclassified per design decision -- allocator consumes measured merge-damage tables (F_S/F_B/F_R/F_P grids); V2_E4 characterizes Gaussian->merge transfer anisotropy, not gated. See V2_E4_resolution.

V2_E4_resolution.statement: The original V2_E4 slope=0.35 (Gaussian-sensitivity predictor D_pred_marginal) reflects Gaussian->merge transfer ANISOTROPY across blocks, not an additivity-structure failure: E4b's measured-damage predictor (P_damage_measured, summing matching F_S single-point D_mse) recovers slope=1.149, R²=0.9993 (n=4 valid F_M configs); the two uniform_r8/r16 configs are NaN by design (even blocks outside the F_S grid).

eps_abs_rescale_provenance.note: one-time post-hoc rescale of E4_raw.csv (197/196 CLS-inclusion off-by-one); no re-sweep performed. rescaled_this_run=False means the data was already on the 196 basis when this cell ran (a fresh sweep with the fixed source, or a CSV already corrected previously).

notes: eps_abs was corrected post-hoc from a 197*384 to a 196*384 per-element divisor (CLS is never a merge candidate, so the cost only ever ranges over 196 patch tokens); all T, D_pred, D_pred_marginal, and in_regime values in E4_raw.csv and the regenerated rho_curves.png/merge_transfer.png reflect the corrected 196 basis. damage_vs_r.png and ward_vs_bipartite.png were regenerated unchanged (D_mse-only, unaffected by eps_abs). schedule_additivity_measured.png and E4b_additivity_reanalysis.json are also unaffected, since P_damage_measured is built entirely from measured D_mse.
